Stellar Discovery
Trust Layer

From an approved payment
to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, and two independent buyer operators. T2 operates the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators; T3 establishes both merchant installations on mainnet under their reviewed production configurations. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in its customer’s application. We commission a complete recurring task: an authorized source or query, its selected population and period, the useful report, file or application result, and the engineer who will maintain the service. The commissioning payer buys that installation and handover; the independent buyer pays for its useful resource. These roles can belong to different organizations.

For an analyst, completion means the entire selected population with its original units, time basis and usable report. For an agent application, it means the approved result within its aggregate task budget. A task spanning paid pages remains open until every agreed page is received. A prepaid call retains the selected pass and its consumed allowance when defaults change. The merchant connects those completed results to its offer, fulfillment and accounting. This makes a purchase usable in the customer’s continuing work.

A public Base implementation report describes two settled USDC payments while the resource remained absent from Bazaar discovery after twenty-four hours. A separate operator later reported successful indexing after new settlements and described the facilitator’s extension-response diagnostics. These first-party accounts distinguish payment, discovery and usable service delivery, supplying cross-ecosystem implementation learning for our Stellar integration. Original report and operator comment.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies native payment authorization and settlement for the customer’s reviewed operation. In the x402 Exact Stellar flow, the buyer signs a Soroban authorization entry for a token transfer with its payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. The facilitator submits the authorization under the selected network and fee policy. Sponsored settlement lets the buyer pay in the selected supported token while the facilitator covers the transaction fee. Existing Stellar wallets, token contracts and payment services provide this native foundation.

The merchant and buyer workspaces retain the HTTP endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request-body identity, selected source or query, and accepted payment option. Their approval and signer integration check the original operation before dispatch. The retained purchase then connects the native transfer to its complete received output and required fulfillment. Buyers keep wallet and aggregate spending authority; merchants keep control of resources, terms and order actions. The grant applies these native-payment and application responsibilities to the selected customers’ actual installations.

The ledger records the transfer; the private workspaces retain the source selection, request, complete output and fulfillment history. The original transaction identity connects these records so an interrupted delivery can continue from its settled purchase. The maintained native signer and facilitator compose the existing x402 packages and token contracts. The facilitator already accepts explicit testnet or pubnet configuration, allowed assets and recipients, fee ceilings, distinct signing accounts and admission/drain controls. The funded deployment supplies the selected operators’ actual network, RPC, fee policy and operating configuration. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model. Native signer · Facilitator operation

The current Stellar x402 documentation identifies the hosted Vellar endpoint as testnet-only. Each installation selects its actual scheme, network, asset and payment requirements. T2 uses two compatible testnet configurations for the same useful service; T3 uses each merchant’s reviewed mainnet-capable configuration.

The contribution is a reusable source-to-customer operating workflow. The completed HPD development example received all 144 selected rows through two paid pages, linked both transfers, and reopened the complete CSV/JSONL edition with source and accounting. The limited paid-query response reopened its 100 returned rows and 14 columns in another receiving directory. The maintained browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces use each product’s original saved state. The funded installations apply this complete-result and maintenance workflow to independent customer services.

We propose Open Track for these reusable merchant-and-buyer capabilities. The six packages develop the selected source/receiving adaptations, independent deployment, monitoring and recovery in the existing architecture. A retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity; the two-facilitator testnet package therefore includes the actual registration and payment-policy work for one service with the same schema, source population and useful output. Published implementation improvements make that work reusable. Independent complete purchases, returning buyers and installations another engineer can operate measure its value to Stellar.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

Select and publish. The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.

Connect the source. Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.

Approve and pay. The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.

Settle and receive. The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.

Use and account. The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.

Recover and hand over. Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are included in the 50-hour/$4,750 response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observation sources, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

It covers changed offers or approvals, incorrect payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, lost observation and restoration of the wrong generation. The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Both retain notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery states, response/recovery times, corrections and the receiving engineer’s reopening after restart. Monitoring gaps remain visible until observation resumes.

MeasureCounting and acceptance
Completed purchaseOne distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Deduplicate transactions per network; retain asset amounts and fees separately.
Prepaid purchaseCount the settled pass once, with at least one agreed operation and complete accepted output. Further calls and allowance units are usage. An unused pass retains unfinished fulfillment; a replacement needs its own settlement and first useful completion.
Complete customer taskReceive and accept every agreed page, file or application result. Retain started tasks, aggregate cost and unfinished coverage beside individual priced requests.
Independent and returning buyersCount the accountable organization/person across its agents and wallets. Both merchants need independent use. Return use requires a distinct qualifying purchase on another UTC day.
Two facilitatorsComplete the same useful service, schema, source population and output through each independent operator, preserving the actual terms and financial result.
Recovery and handoverContinue original requests and financial outcomes; reopen selected files/history, reconcile later operations and complete the maintainer’s support case.

The funded targets are ten completed purchases in total across the two independent buyers in T2’s seven-day window and thirty in total in T3’s fourteen-day window. The completed Queens HPD acquisition contains two paid pages of 100 and 44 rows: two purchases totaling 20,000 native testnet stroops and one complete 144-row customer task, with fees separate. The eight-unit prepaid example is one 10,000-stroop purchase whose first useful request consumed two units and retained six. A later allowance call records its task and units; a new payment records another purchase. Reopening the saved result continues its original task and purchase.

The seven- and fourteen-day cohorts retain all attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Original first-attempt time determines purchase-window membership; native settlement, complete accepted output and any applicable order completion must occur within that same window. The observation cutoff can retain later observations without moving a later completion into the earlier window. The reviewed customer/operator declarations establish independence; team activity retains its own baseline.

For each installation, compare the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same source population or period and expected output: active effort, manual corrections, time to useful output, acceptance and unresolved work. Pricing measurements retain quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage. Commercial measures use agreed scope, accepted milestones, issued fees, actual collections and support effort from the original workorder/accounting records.

For a stated evaluation period, direct labor value is completed tasks multiplied by active hours saved per comparable task and the customer's stated hourly value, less the one-time implementation fee and total incremental provider, hosting, payment and support costs during that period. Record those inputs with the original workorder; the same calculation gives the effort reduction needed to recover the fee. Compare the initial result, the following source period and an independent maintainer's change or recovery.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

Bryce is accountable for allocating contributors and operating resources to the six packages. The retained resource study uses 400 hours over 150 days. Its lowest examined timely allocation is 25 engineering hours plus eight integration/handover hours per week. This is a modeled allocation; named contributor availability and payment arrangements are being finalized against the actual award date.

SCF’s four payments would be $3,800 at award acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective deliverables are approved. These payment amounts differ from tranche delivery costs. The USD-equivalent award is paid in XLM; the XLM quantity uses CF XLMUSD_RR, or SDF’s selected qualifying alternative, reported on the actual award payment day, under the Official Rules.

Grant and accepted commercial work share one contributor capacity plan. A commissioned workshare adds its actual hours, dependencies and acceptance dates; available hours are allocated once. Bryce reconciles the combined schedule and expected collections before agreeing dated work, using separately named capacity or agreed timing changes. The maintained Grant Operations workspace keeps supplier work and invoices, reviewed statement cash movements and dated installation capacity in the same retained grant case, with complete source-linked reports and customer receiving.

The resource model makes the working-capital requirement explicit. With its labor-accrual assumptions, additional peak cash is $17,250 at a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days. Opening cash and a committed bridge or contributor deferral have not been entered. Actual available funds, client collections and agreed contributor payment timing must cover the modeled requirement before the corresponding delivery commitments are made.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding payment. For an anticipated delay, we will obtain SDF’s written acknowledgment before the original deadline and use a revised deadline only when confirmed in writing.

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source deployment and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation and separately scoped care. Workorders retain delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining estimate, keeping the grant focused on the agreed prospective Stellar development.
